title: Transformers without heavy mathematics
goal: Explain tokens, attention weights, masking and model roles.
case: A document assistant must choose what earlier words matter when drafting a sentence.
terms: A model processes pieces of text represented as IDs. A word may use more than one token.
Each query uses scores to weight available tokens; the weighted combination carries contextual information.
A decoder mask prevents a token from using future tokens while generating left to right.
Encoders read inputs; decoders generate; encoder-decoder models read then generate from a separate component.
steps: Tokenize a tiny three-word classroom example
Compute normalized attention weights from simple scores
Apply a mask to hide a future word
Compare an encoder and a decoder task
example: If the third token is future text, its masked weight becomes 0.
misconception: Attention weights are a complete explanation of a model decision.
correction: They show one internal weighting operation; they do not prove causal importance or factual correctness.
change: Mask the last token and recompute the weights.
metric: Weights sum to one over visible tokens
lab: Compute attention for three tokens and explain one mask.
output: Annotated attention table and one model-role choice.
reading: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need
